moments.title: Battle of the Sexes
moments.who: Billie Jean King vs Bobby Riggs, Houston Astrodome
moments.body: On 20 September 1973, 29-year-old Billie Jean King defeats 55-year-old former Wimbledon champion Bobby Riggs 6-4, 6-3, 6-3 in front of 30,492 spectators (still a US tennis record) and an estimated 90 million TV viewers. Riggs had defeated Margaret Court 6-2 6-1 earlier in 1973. King later said: 'I thought it would set us back 50 years if I didn't win that match.'
moments.takeaway: A single tennis match watched by 90 million people shifted attitudes about women's sport in a way no policy could match.

now.title: Women's tennis today
now.body: King founded the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) in 1973. Prize money parity reached Wimbledon (2007), with Venus Williams a leading voice. The WTA's 2021 stand against China after the Peng Shuai disappearance was a rare modern example of a sport governing body confronting a major state.
now.open_questions: Why has tennis achieved prize-money parity at majors while most other sports have not?

reflection: King also founded the Women's Sports Foundation (1974) and was the first openly lesbian top-tier athlete (outed in 1981; she lost endorsements estimated at $2 million). Her 2014 USTA recognition came decades late.
